literal_operations_in_order.exact_old_utf8: Let h be one four-dimensional one-handle attached compatibly to an oriented four-dimensional stage, with feet in a connected compact oriented three-dimensional base N. The stage orientation makes the normal bundle of each closed core orientable; its rank-three frame can be closed as in [F2].
literal_operations_in_order.exact_new_utf8: Let h be one four-dimensional one-handle with feet in a connected compact oriented three-dimensional base N, with the orientable closed-core normal bundle required in the Statement. This condition is independent of the joining base arc. Indeed, the collar $N\times I$ is oriented, so transport along every base arc has positive determinant in oriented frames; the only possible orientation sign on a closed core comes from the fixed two-foot transition of h. Thus both $\gamma_B=A'\cup B$ and $\gamma_{B'}=A'\cup B'$ have orientable rank-three normal bundles, even when the arcs represent different relative homotopy classes. An orientable rank-three real bundle over a circle is a product: trivialize it over a cut interval and join its positive-determinant endpoint transition to the identity by a path in $GL^+(3,\mathbb R)$, exactly as in [F2]. Start with the prescribed rank-two arc-tube frame plus the collar-normal line and extend it along the handle core using the common foot germs. This supplies the actual closed product frames needed for the framed-circle trade. Keep these frames throughout: no homotopy between the two possible rank-three framing classes, and no replacement of a prescribed integral strip framing, is being assumed. The orientation is needed only on this collar-and-handle comparison neighborhood, not on the rest of the surrounding stage. Apply the local cancellation and strip-routing charts of [F1] inside that oriented neighborhood; their product constructions and the [F2] surgery charts extend by the identity outside their supports.
